newsitem.title: USA: Camden Property comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Camden Property comfortable with estimates.

text.p: Camden Property Trust chairman Richard Campo said on Thursday he was comfortable with estimates the company would have operating cashflow equivalent to $0.64 a share in the second quarter and $2.60 for the year.
"We're comfortable with that," he said of the estimates, compiled by First Call, in an interview after the company's annual meeting.
Operating cashflow, or funds from operations, is the primary measure of financial performance for real estate investment trusts such as Camden and is forecast by analysts instead of net income.
Camden had cashflow equivalent to $0.60 a share in the second quarter of 1996 and $2.40 for the full year on revenues of $111.6 million.

Camden has 35,300 apartments in 12 cities, with a number of new projects underway. Campo said rental rates, which averaged $0.75 a square foot at the end of 1996, should rise three percent to five percent this year.
"We're able to do a little better than inflation because the markets are strong," he said. The company had an overall occupancy rate of 94 percent in 1996.
